skill.summary: Execute Python-based data analysis and reporting tasks in an isolated sandbox workflow.
skill.author: CK991357

security_audit.summary: Static findings were reviewed against source context. The flagged patterns are documentation examples, markdown formatting, mathematical cookbook snippets, or explicit prohibited-operation warnings rather than active malicious behavior.

remediation.issue: Forbidden-operation examples include dangerous strings such as exec, os.system, and /etc/passwd.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the warning, but rewrite examples in descriptive text or non-executable pseudocode to reduce scanner noise and copy-paste risk.

remediation.issue: Many markdown backticks are detected as shell execution patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearer prose around code fences and label examples as sandbox-only guidance, not host commands.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on sandbox controls for safe Python execution.
remediation.suggestion: Publish only with a compatible sandbox that blocks network access, system commands, dynamic execution, and host filesystem access.

content.user_title: Run Python Data Workflows in a Sandbox
content.value_statement: Data and reporting tasks often need repeatable Python workflows with clear output rules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through sandboxed analysis, charts, and downloadable document generation.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to read and write workspace files in a sandboxed data directory.
Provides patterns for Pandas, DuckDB, SciPy, SymPy, and machine learning workflows.
Guides chart creation with Matplotlib, Seaborn, Graphviz, and NetworkX.
Shows how to generate Excel, Word, PDF, and PowerPoint outputs for download.
Documents memory, file persistence, and multi-step session workflow practices.
limitations: Requires a compatible Python sandbox tool to execute code.
Network access is described as disabled, so remote data fetching is not supported.
Large files may require chunked processing to avoid memory limits.
Generated files must follow the documented output protocol.

use_cases.title: Analyze Business Data
use_cases.description: Clean spreadsheets, aggregate metrics, create charts, and export a summary workbook.

use_cases.title: Prototype Machine Learning Models
use_cases.description: Prepare data, train simple models, compare metrics, and visualize model performance.

use_cases.title: Generate Automated Reports
use_cases.description: Create Word, PDF, Excel, or PowerPoint reports from analysis outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Python sandbox workflow to inspect my uploaded dataset, summarize columns, identify missing values, and report key statistics.

prompt_templates.title: Create Charts and Insights
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the sales data in the sandbox, create clear charts, explain the main trends, and include any data quality concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Downloadable Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a downloadable business report from the analysis results, including tables, charts, and a short executive summary.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Step Modeling Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the sandbox to clean the dataset, train a baseline model, evaluate it, tune parameters, and summarize limitations and next steps.

output_examples.input: Analyze a sales spreadsheet and explain regional performance.
output: Summary of total sales by region

output_examples.input: Create a PDF report from customer survey results.
Train a simple prediction model and explain performance.
output: Plain-language notes about limits and bias risks

best_practices: Keep source data in the documented workspace directory when possible.
Use chunked processing or efficient formats for large datasets.
Ask for charts and reports in separate steps when the analysis is complex.
anti_patterns: Do not expect the sandbox to access network resources.
Do not process sensitive files without confirming data handling requirements.
Do not generate large files without checking memory and output limits.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Python by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance for a compatible sandbox tool that executes Python code.

faq.question: Can it create downloadable files?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents output patterns for Excel, Word, PDF, and PowerPoint files.

faq.question: Can it fetch data from the internet?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes network access as disabled in the sandbox environment.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What data formats are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers common table files, text data, charts, and generated office documents.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production automation?
faq.answer: It is best for guided analysis and report generation, not unattended production pipelines.
